OET Writing
Layout:
   1. If the recipient name is given in the writing task, for example:
Dr Malcom Still (recipient full name)
Rheumatologist (speciality,General Practitioner,community
Nurse,...) City Hospital
Newtown
(one line)
13 June 2020 (Today’s date)
(one line)
Dear Dr Still, (surname)
(one line)
Re: Mr David Taylor, DOB: 01 August 1965 or, aged 55 or, 55 years of age

Yours sincerely,
(two lines)
Doctor

   2. If the recipient name is not given, for
example: The Admitting Officer (The Cardiologist)
The Emergency Department
Children’s Hospital
Newtown
(one line)
18 January 2014
(one line)
Dear Sir/Madam,or (Dear Admitting Officer,)if he is not a
 doctor or Dear Doctor
(one line)
Re: Joshua Vance, DOB: 17 November 2013

Yours faithfully,
(two lines)
Doctor




                                                               NOet
 
Types of the letters:
    1) Referral letter:
          ● Normal
Writing task: Using the information in the case notes, write a referral
letter to …..(specialist/new GP)
    ❏ Introduction
Thank you for seeing Mrs Santini, a 67-year-old widow, who has
worsening osteoarthritis of her both knee joints and a Becker’s cyst in
the right knee joint. Your expert assessment and management would be
valued.

I am writing to request a review for assessment and rehydration of
Joshua, a full-term breastfed infant, who has constipation and
mild dehydration.

  ❏ Chronological style of the visits => organisation of the letter
  ❏ Past medical hx and current medication
  ❏ Social and Family history
  ❏ Conclusion

          ● Urgent
    ❏ Introduction
I am writing to refer MrX, a 52-year-old builder, who has adenocarcinoma
of the ascending colon. Your urgent assessment,including a colonoscopy,
and management would be valued.

I am writing to urgently refer MrX,....
I am writing to request (an) urgent assessment and management of …..

Thank you for seeing Mr Knowles, a 68-year-old retired management
consultant, who requires urgent investigation of his upper GI symptoms.



  ❏ Today visit
  ❏ Previous visits
  ❏ Past medical hx and current medication



                                                                  NOet
 
❏ Social and Family history
   ❏ Conclusion

**Important note:
1)Provisional diagnosis: who I suspect has (disease)
  Definitive diagnosis: who has(disease/symptom)
2)If the patient's age is less than 18 years old, we don't put the title( Ms,
Mrs,..) before the name and we write the first name in the letter.
3)Regarding the order of the visits, you should structure the letter in
order of importance to the reader. This could be chronological, thematic
or in an emergency, with the most recent information first so they can
understand the need for the urgency.

    2) Discharge letter
          ● To patient’s GP
Writing task: Using the information in the case notes, write a discharge
letter to MrX’s GP,....

   ❏ Introduction
I am writing with regard to MrX, who is being discharged from our
hospital into your care after treatment for (disease). He requires now
your follow-up with his medication.

MrX was admitted on (Date) for the purpose of (total left knee
replacement surgery) after having a car accident. He is now ready for
discharge and follow-up into your care.

MrX is being discharged into your care today for follow-up treatment.
He was admitted on (Date) for total left knee replacement surgery due a
car accident.



   ❏ On admission +post op
   ❏ During hospitalisation
   ❏ Discharge medication
   ❏ Conclusion



                                                                     NOet
 
● To another health allies
Writing task: Using the information in the case notes, write a discharge
letter to Mr Graham, medical director of nursing facility…

   ❏ Introduction
Mr McCarthy is being discharged to your facility today for (acute care
and physiotherapy)/(pulmonary rehabilitation). He was admitted on
(date) for (right below knee amputation/etc) due to a diabetic foot ulcer.



  ❏ On admission +post op
  ❏ During hospitalisation
  ❏ Medical hx and treatment/discharge medication****not necessary
    to write all of them +no medical jargon.
  ❏ Social and Family hx (relevant only)
  ❏ Owing to MrX’s current condition, he requires…(nursing
    assistance)


    3) Transfer Letter
Writing task: Using the information in the case notes, write a transfer
letter to the ICU doctor.

   ❏ Introduction
I am writing to request an urgent ICU transfer of Ms Y who is
presenting with severe respiratory distress, possibly due to COVID-19.

  ❏ The order as a referral letter (urgent or normal)


**Important note:

Avoid writing medical details and terminology (if the recipient is not a
doctor: occupational therapist, community nurse, admitting officer,...)




                                                                     NOet
 
4) Update letter
Writing task: Using the information given in the case notes, write a
letter to Dr X, the doctor who referred (patient name), to update
her/him on the patient's status and follow-up treatment that may be
required in the future.

   ❏ Introduction:
I am writing to update you regarding Ms Garcia, who has been
referred with suspected meningitis. Your ongoing follow-up would be
greatly valued, as her diagnosis is now confirmed.

  ❏ Visits after the referral ( mainly one visit)+ O/E + investigations
    + treatment.
  ❏ Here, it is very important not to include any data that the patient’s
    GP knows; for example, patient age/job (in introduction),
    past medical hx, social and family hx.
  ❏ Conclusion


Social,medical and Family history:
It is better here to use a complex sentence, for example:
Mrs Mills, who quit smoking 20 years ago, has a strong family history
of myocardial infarction, hypertension and type 2 DM.
or
Ms Day, who smokes and drinks moderately, has a stressful lifestyle.
She has been on oral contraceptive pills since 2013. She has no family
history of migraine or headache.




                                                                  NOet
 
please note :

Do not write as He is a heavy / (ex-) smoker or drinks heavily as it is
judgmental (oet website).




                     General advice on writing
1) The dates in the letter should be written in full (07/11/2010).
2) There is *no space* before Thank you... or I am writing to....
3)some verbs need to be written in perfect tense as they have a
gradual action like( improve, deteriorate, worsen) so you have to
write; for example:
His condition has improved or has worsened.
4) Never write " the list of medication is attached " unless it's written in
the case note.
5)Be careful of these common spelling and preposition mistakes:
a- advice is uncountabe-noun and advise is the verb.
b- compliant with (medication or any sort of treatment) and a
complaint of (symptom).
c- compliant *with* and adherent *to* .
6) Re: Mr X, aged 65 with small (a).
7) The verb present when means come, never used in perfect tense ( Mr
X has presented today with...  ).
8) l would appreciate *it* do not forget (it), do not write ( I would
appreciate it if you could...   )
9) However and Therefore are preferred to use at the beginning of the
sentence.
10) Surgery is uncountable and operation is countable, so do not write (
He underwent a left knee replacement surgery      ).
11) Numbers less than ten are better to be written in letters ( He has a
two-week history of…)


                                                                        NOet
 
12) In spite of/ despite are followed by noun or gerund (verb+ing),
although is followed by verb clause.
13) The verb report mainly is followed by the past perfect as the events in
the case note are mainly in past simple, so you will write :
He reported that he had developed back pain.
Or
He reported having developed back pain (having + past participle)
14) Blood pressure is uncountable except if it is followed by (of):
On examination, she was afebrile with a blood pressure of 148/98 and a
BMI over 30.
15) If there are multiple unnecessary visits, you can summarize them as
the following examples:
Mr Weir had seen me twice over the last couple of months complaining
of fatigue and stress.
Or
Mr Jones has been seeing a physiotherapist for the past three months.
He currently walks for 30 minutes per day although he reports that this
is quite tiring.


16) The verb attend when means present, it should be used with an
object, so do not write (Mr X attended with a complaint of …..  )
The correct is (he attended my clinic /our hospital…).




                                                                      NOet
